title: Goal synthesis & postmortem — micro-OKR log
body:
Context:
This is my lightweight, runnable personal OKR / KPI notebook — meant to live on my laptop and in Drive as a scratchpad. It combines a short-term micro-OKR (2 weeks), a habit budget, and an experiment/retro cadence. Use this when I'm too lazy for a formal doc but need an accountable record.

Goals (2-week micro-OKR):
- Objective: Increase reliable product demo readiness and reduce scramble time before customer calls.
  - KR1: Move demo warm-up checklist to a single runnable script + 80% success in dev environment (manual -> scripted) — baseline: 2/5 successful dry-runs. Target: 4/5.
  - KR2: Cut demo rollback and recovery time from average 9m -> <= 4m (measure with timestamps in meeting notes).
  - KR3: Capture 3 reproducible failure modes and add checks (exit codes / logs) to prevent them.

Primary metrics I'm tracking this sprint:
- Dry-run success rate: 2/5 -> aim 4/5.
- Mean recovery time (minutes): 9 -> target <=4.
- Number of automated checks added: 0 -> target >=3.
- Focus hours/week (blocked, deep work): >=10h (measured by calendar blocks).

Hypotheses / why these matter:
- If the demo warm-up is reproducible and scriptable, cognitive load during calls drops and we avoid the "fumble" effect that reduces perceived reliability.
- Small automation wins compound: each check that converts a manual step saves ~1–2 minutes per call and reduces error rates.

Plan / experiments for next 14 days:
1) Script the warm-up: convert the 7-step manual checklist into a shell/python script that verifies environment variables, model access, network checks, and a sample inference run. Make it idempotent and run locally. (Estimate: 4–6h)
2) Add health-exit flags: fail early with clear logs if key services not available (model endpoint auth, disk mount, quantized model load). (Estimate: 2–3h)
3) Timebox daily 60–90 minute "demo prep" session X3 in week 1 to iterate script and record times.
4) Create a tiny failure-mode doc (2 columns: symptom -> repro steps -> guard) and add to repo README.
5) Postmortem format: for each failed dry-run, capture timestamp, step failed, log excerpt, fix applied, and time-to-fix.

Quick schedule (rough):
- Mon: outline script + repo scaffolding (1h).
- Tue/Wed: implement core checks + run 2 dry-runs.
- Thu: add log/exit formatting + run 3 dry-runs.
- Fri: retro notes and update README.

Weekly check-in template (for my sanity):
- Wins this week:
  - Script prototype runs locally without manual tweaks (2/3 dry-runs passed).
  - Added an early-exit check for missing KMS creds.
- Misses / blockers:
  - Unreliable network dependency to internal model registry — need to shadow with cached model artifact.
- Actions for next week:
  - Add local cached-package fallback and measure recovery time.
  - Pair with Marco for a flaky network debug session.

Retrospective notes (live):
- Observed failure pattern: 60% of failures are due to stale env vars in shell history — silly but real. Action: add an env-check step that prints non-sensitive indicator and exits if mismatch.
- Social friction: during early tests, I was embarrassed by repeated restarts in front of PMs. That matters to confidence. Quick wins (scripts) help reduce shame and increase probability of shipping demos.

Decision journal (why I chose these KRs):
- Chose demo reliability as top objective because demos are currently responsible for >30% of my perceived weekly context switches and highest anxiety events. Reducing friction yields both time and psychological ROI.
- Focus hours target is soft commitment — if I hit it I get compounding progress; if not, signals to reduce scope.

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- Script repository with README and CI check exists.
- Dry-run success >=4/5 for 3 consecutive runs.
- Recovery time median <=4m measured across 5 simulated failure runs.
- 3 guard checks merged into main branch.

Notes-to-self (informal, messy):
- Keep the script tiny — avoid overengineering. If I find I'm spending >10h, reduce scope: aim for 2 checks first.
- When pairing with Marco, focus on the flaky network (he knows the proxy voodoo).
- Put a tiny celebratory ritual when I hit KR1 (small internal reward).

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: infra team may change the internal registry API; mitigation: pin a cached artifact in repo with clear TTL.
- Risk: automating checks could create false confidence (they pass but don't reflect real-world edge cases). Mitigate by adding one randomized noisy test.

Mini-postmortem (end of sprint template):
- What I committed to: list KRs.
- What I actually did: bullet list.
- Outcome vs. target: numbers and short commentary.
- Root causes for misses: 1–3 bullets.
- Next-step hypothesis for next sprint.

Random heuristics I want to remember:
- 80/20 the demo: if 2 checks block 80% of failures, ship them first.
- Measure before you celebrate: timestamps matter.
- Make failures visible in the first 90s of script run.

Log (running) — examples from dry-runs:
- 2024-11-06 09:12:12 — dry-run 1 — fail at step 3: model load (exit code 23). Fix: re-symlink quantized model. Time to fix: 12m.
- 2024-11-07 14:04:02 — dry-run 2 — pass. Script took 2m34s total.
- 2024-11-08 11:20:44 — dry-run 3 — fail at step 1: missing ENV_X_TOKEN. Fix: update local .env loader. Time to fix: 5m.

Action items (next 7 days):
- [ ] Py script: add net/model checks (Harper) — due Tue.
- [ ] Add README + CI check (Harper + Aisha) — due Thu.
- [ ] Cached artifact fallback + TTL policy (Marco) — due Fri.
- [ ] Pair debugging session (Harper + Marco) — schedule 1h this week.

Closing note: keep this doc messy on purpose. If I polish it, I will lose the velocity of quick fixes. Archive the final postmortem to Confluence only after I have a clean commit and measurement artifacts.

---
Small gratitude entry: got a helpful tip from Aisha on log formatting that saved 3m on the first fix.

End of scratchpad.
